- **Strengths:** Enhances accuracy and image quality of 2D-texture based rendering; allows separate updates for different components at different resolutions; avoids striping artifacts in DVR variants [S1, unofficial][S2].

The claim consists of three parts, all of which are explicitly supported by the provided evidence: 1) 'Enhances accuracy and image quality of 2D-texture based rendering' is supported by Source [S1], which states the approach is designed to 'enhance the accuracy and the image quality of the 2D-texture based approach'. 2) 'Allows separate updates for different components at different resolutions' is supported by Source [S1], which explains that keeping components in separate textures allows illumination and fog to be updated interactively while preserving high resolution for the color texture. 3) 'Avoids striping artifacts in DVR variants' is supported by Source [S2], which notes that maintaining a constant step size avoids 'striping artifacts caused by nonuniform sampling step' in a DVR algorithm using multitexturing.

It addresses the limitations of single-texture approaches by allowing separate updates for different components (e.g., color, light map, fog map) at different resolutions, whereas a single texture maps all components together [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that multi-texturing allows separate updates for different components (e.g., color, light map, fog map) at different resolutions, whereas a single texture maps all components together. The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly states: 'The traditional texture map, which contains the object's color, is supplemented by two multi-textures, which store the pre-computed illumination (light map) and fog density (fog map)... On the other hand the color texture will be highly detailed, while for the light and the fog map low resolution might be sufficient. Keeping all these components in separate textures allows illumination and fog density to be updated interactively while preserving high resolution for the color texture.' This directly supports every part of the claim.
